questions.prompt: Using put-call parity, what put price matches a call priced at 8.92?
questions.context: S = K = 100, r = 2%, q = 0, T = 1y; ignore transaction costs.

questions.prompt: How many shares should a desk sell to delta-hedge long calls initially?
questions.context: 1,000 calls, multiplier 100 shares, Delta = 0.54; long calls have positive delta.
questions.explanation: Long delta is 1,000 × 100 × 0.54 = 54,000 shares, so the hedge sells 54,000.

questions.prompt: What is the second-order gamma P&L in the displayed scenario?

questions.prompt: What is the vega P&L for a three-point volatility increase?

questions.prompt: What is the approximate PV of this payer swap?
questions.context: Notional 100m EUR, fixed 3.20%, par 3.00%, annuity 4.55.
questions.explanation: Payer PV ≈ (par − fixed) × annuity × notional = (3.00% − 3.20%) × 4.55 × 100m = −910,000 EUR.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate DV01 of the same payer swap?
questions.context: Notional 100m EUR and annuity 4.55; DV01 is stated per basis point.

questions.prompt: What is the payer swap P&L for a +10bp parallel move?
questions.context: Payer DV01 = +45,500 EUR/bp; use the local linear approximation.
questions.explanation: P&L ≈ DV01 × 10 = 45,500 × 10 = +455,000 EUR; a payer benefits when rates rise.

questions.prompt: What discount factor follows from a one-year annual par rate of 3%?
questions.context: Use the simple annual par-coupon convention shown in the exercise.

questions.prompt: What is the bootstrapped two-year discount factor?
questions.context: DF(1Y) = 0.9708738 and the two-year annual par rate is 3.20%.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate DV01 of this long bond position?

questions.prompt: What is the linear P&L for a +25bp yield shock on the long bond?
questions.context: DV01 = 17,000 EUR/bp; ignore convexity for this small-shock estimate.
questions.explanation: A long bond loses when yields rise: −17,000 × 25 = −425,000 EUR.

questions.prompt: What is the one-day 95% parametric VaR?
questions.context: Portfolio 20m EUR; daily volatility 2%; one-sided z-score 1.645.
questions.explanation: VaR = 20m × 0.02 × 1.645 = 658,000 EUR; this is not a worst-case loss.

questions.prompt: What is the CDS CS01 before applying the position sign?
questions.context: Notional 50m EUR; risky annuity 4.2; CS01 is per 1bp.

questions.prompt: What is the absolute spread-shock PV move for +25bp widening?
questions.context: CS01 = 21,000 EUR/bp; report the move before buyer/seller position sign.
questions.explanation: Absolute move = 21,000 × 25 = 525,000 EUR; protection-buyer/seller sign is separate.

questions.prompt: What is the payoff at spot 1.20 if the barrier was never touched?
questions.context: Down-and-out EUR/USD call; strike 1.10; notional EUR 10m; payoff is in USD.
questions.explanation: (1.20 − 1.10) × EUR 10m = 1,000,000 USD, assuming no knock-out.

questions.prompt: What implied volatility matches the displayed ATM call price?
questions.context: Call = 8.00; S = K = 100; r = 2%; T = 0.5y; Newton starts at 20%.
questions.explanation: Using Black-Scholes vega per vol unit, Newton-Raphson converges in four iterations to 26.73%.

questions.prompt: What does the reported 95% confidence interval communicate?
questions.context: Asian call estimate 5.36; standard error 0.03; interval [5.31, 5.41].
questions.explanation: The interval describes Monte Carlo sampling uncertainty under the declared simulation convention; it is not a live quote.

questions.prompt: Which risk-neutral probability is plausible for this four-step CRR tree?
